explanation: The V32I substitution introduces a bulkier, branched side chain in closer spatial proximity to darunavir's binding interactions, likely creating a steric clash that destabilizes inhibitor accommodation within the S2 subpocket. Since valine-to-isoleucine represents an increase in hydrophobic volume (addition of a methyl group on the β-carbon), this unfavorable geometric constraint disrupts the precise fit darunavir requires for optimal van der Waals contacts with the protease backbone and nearby residues, thereby reducing binding affinity.
